claims.text: A minor alloying addition can promote in situ formation of a lubricious, temperature-responsive oxide phase in CoCrFeNi.
Formation of the proposed oxide phase will improve the wide-temperature tribological performance of CoCrFeNi.
A few atomic percent of Re or another oxide-forming element can enable development of a self-adaptive lubricious oxide during sliding.
Re is a refractory metal that is potentially suitable for forming a lubricious oxide in this application.
The alloying addition will generate a fine, stable oxide phase in situ at the sliding interface.
The interfacial oxide phase will function as a solid lubricant.
At lower temperatures, the modified alloy will retain a microstructure similar to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
At elevated temperatures, the introduced element will oxidize preferentially.
Preferential oxidation will produce a continuous lubricious oxide film.
The continuous oxide film will reduce friction and wear.
The self-adaptive oxide film will maintain low friction over a broad temperature range.
Near 800 °C, the modified alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than baseline CoCrFeNi.
Near 800 °C, the modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than baseline CoCrFeNi.
At lower temperatures, the modified alloy will provide tribological performance at least comparable to baseline CoCrFeNi.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing coefficient of friction as temperature rises.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing wear rate as temperature rises.
The proposed improvement will be effective under moderate-to-high sliding loads in oxidizing environments.
Very low or very high oxygen partial pressures may diminish the proposed improvement.
Loads beyond the tested range may diminish the proposed improvement.
